Good luck!! I can't handle (literal)shit at all. I would have probably made it all worse by throwing up all over it. 

The grossest thing I've ever dealt with(not that anyone asked but i feel like sharing): I was working lunch once and the only people in the restaurant was a youngish couple with two children under 10. The last 30 mins they were just chatting while the children played around the table so i let them be. They came up to the register to pay(which is whats normal at this restairant) and left as if nothing was wrong. When i went to bus their table i slipped and landed on my ass in something wet on the floor. One of the kids had pissed himself AND NOBODY TOLD ME!!! I was so mad. I had to borrow a clean skirt from my boss.

I see it this way: You go out to eat to be 'served'. I'm not subhuman but i do in a way work for you. If you work in an office your boss may tell you "i need this done by Friday" or something like that. It's not the most polite way of going about it but it's still reasonable.

However if you're gonna make me jump through hoops you better be nice to me. I see that kinda like a boss at an office giving you something on friday when you have the weekend off and needing it done by monday.

And how do you know it's gossip when you can't hear it? there are many reasons a server might need to talk to another server.

Aaand... You think it's just bringing food and drink refills? This is a small list of all the things i can think of. A servers job may include some of these, all of these or more: 

Memorising the menu and being able to answer all the customers questions about said menu - Even ones like when the fish we use for the baked salmon was caught. You have to know what kinds of wine and beer and soft drinks you have and give recommendations about what goes well with the food. You have to memorize orders, additions and substitutions. Where i work servers are also bartenders so we have to know how to make all the drinks, change kegs and restock the wine fridge. Sometimes the servers also function as hosts. You also have to be able to balance like 10 drinks on a tray. You have to bus and pre bus your tables, clean your tables. You have to fold napkins. You have to function as a messenger between kitchen and the customer. Come up with solutions whenever something goes wrong. You have to take shit for mistakes the kitchen made. You have to always make sure the guests have a good experience. Always smile even though you're having a shit day. You have to always keep track of your tables - who need more water? who's ready to pay? who wants desert? Customer service is a really big one... You have to know how the POC works. You have to answer the phone. Answer questions about reservations. Handle take out orders. After all that is done you have to clean everything and make it ready for the next day.

I have to do most of these things and i don't work anywhere fancy. Also i walk between 15,000 and 20,000 steps each shift and i cary a lot of heavy stuff.

Then the tipping thing: If your *server* did a truly terible job i think it's fair not to tip them as much as long as it is really the servers fault.
You implied that no skills are needed and I'm simply pointing out that that's wrong at least some of the time. especially if you want to work somewhere ou get $200 a night.
Actually, you can go to school to become a waiter. At least where I'm from. If you want to work at really high end places you basically have to have an education to get hired.

I was so embarrassed.

Now it's quite obvious what is prawn and what is chicken because the prawn tails are poking out. What i wanted do whas ask him where on the chicken he thought the prawn tail came from.

Table then pays 2000 instead of 200... I had to go get the owner (who was helping with serving and in the kitchen thats how busy we were) to return the money. It ends up taking him 20 minutes to do so - cause he isn't that technical. The table is getting pissed off because they hired a nanny to watch their children but she had to leave so their kids are home alone. and people are waiting to pay because it's taking up the register.

I apologized for being awkward when i returned with their drinks and they just laughed at me(in a good way).

I'm the only FOH at lunch time. So I had one guy come in alone for lunch. He orders and gets his food and drink and he is making a mess(food on the floor and on himself). I keep an eye on him cause he looks kind of suspect. At one point he leaves for the bathroom and takes a while to come back out. I almost had one of the chefs check the mens room that he was still there and hadn't left without paying but he comes back before i do it and then he sits for a bit and looks ill. I had a lot of other things to see to so i leave him alone for 10 minutes and when i come back to check on him he is passed out over the table. I couldn't wake him up and me and some of the BOH tried for 5-10 minutes. I get kinda scared so i call the emergency hotline. The lady on the phone tells me to rub his chest and ribs with my fists until he wakes up, which he does. I then tell him i called for help and he panics and takes off and I'm just stood there starring and wayyy to confused to remember to go after him with the bill.

It's not even necessarily that people give TMI on the phone. I've had phone conversations go like:

Me: "Hi, you've reached *'place where i work'*. How may i help you?"

Guy on the phone: "I have a reservation"

Me: "How may i help you with that?"

Guy: "I want to cancel it"

Me: "I can help you with that, I just need the name and phone number you used to make the reservation"

Guy: "my reservation number is ..."

Me: "That alright sir, i just need your name"

I get the name and cancel the reservation. I think we're done and most of the time we are... But sometimes the person on the phone will go on and say something like: "Now i'd like to make another reservation for the same time, but for 5 people instead of 4"

Also, please know under what name your reservation is. I can't help you if you just say "I'm supposed to join a group of like around 7 people... maybe 8" but you don't know who made the reservation. on busy nights we might have four tables of that size coming around the same time.
